By Anthony Fenech
Free Press Sports Writer
The Detroit Tigers don't need to wait for Lou Whitaker to become a Hall of Famer.

In their strongest statement on his Cooperstown candidacy, the team announced Tuesday morning they will be retiring Whitaker’s uniform No. 1, which he wore from 1978-1995. Whitaker’s No. 1 will be the ninth retired uniform number in Tigers history.

In 19 seasons, Whitaker hit .276 with 244 home runs, 143 stolen bases and a lifetime on-base percentage of .363 in nearly 10,000 plate appearances. He won the 1984 World Series with the Tigers and was a five-time American League All-Star. Whitaker won four Silver Slugger Awards, three Gold Glove Awards and was the 1978 AL Rookie of the Year.

Whitaker, 62, was denied election to the Baseball Hall of Fame for a second time a week ago: In his only season on the Baseball Writers’ Association of America ballot in 2001, he received 2.9% of the vote, falling short of the 5% threshold to stay on the ballot; and in his first try on the Modern Era veterans’ committee ballot on Dec. 8, he received six votes, six shy of the 12 needed from the 16-man committee.

The Tigers, led by Chairman and CEO Christopher Ilitch — a team which has long held the Hall of Fame as their standard to retire uniform numbers — did not wait but a week to give him the ultimate organizational honor.

Next summer, Whitaker ’s No. 1 will join Charlie Gehringer’s No. 2, Alan Trammell’s No. 3, Hank Greenberg’s No. 5, Al Kaline’s No. 6, Sparky Anderson’s No. 11, Hal Newhouser’s No. 16, Willie Horton’s No. 23 and Jack Morris’ No. 47.

All of those previously retired numbers have been worn by players inducted into the Hall of Fame and Detroit ambassador Willie Horton, who currently serves as a special assistant to general manager Al Avila.

Judged by his 19-season body of work and against those of players previously elected to the Hall of Fame, Whitaker, the longtime Detroit Tigers’ second baseman, is worthy: According to Baseball-Reference.com, Whitaker accrued 75.1 career Wins Above Replacement; only nine position players ahead of him on that list are not in the Hall of Fame, and seven of those are either not yet eligible for induction or have been previously implicated in performance-enhancing drug use.
Whitaker is next eligible for election by the Modern Era committee in 2022.
With Whitaker’s uniform No. 1 out of commission, 21 players wore uniform No. 1 in Tigers history, the last being second baseman Josh Harrison in 2019.
Anthony Fenech
Detroit Free Press
Tigers beat writer
